definitions.explanation: A first-person pronoun belonging to written and elevated style: speeches, literature, mottoes, and set phrases. In ordinary conversation {私|わたし} is used instead.
One's own mind or presence of mind, as opposed to being carried away or absorbed. This sense survives mainly in fixed expressions.

examples.japanese: {我|われ}{思|おも}う、ゆえに{我|われ}あり。
{我|われ}こそはと{思|おも}う{人|ひと}は{手|て}を{挙|あ}げてください。
examples.english: Anyone who thinks they are up to it, please raise your hand.

examples.japanese: {我|われ}なき{時|とき}にも{仕事|しごと}が{続|つづ}くよう、{若|わか}い{人|ひと}を{育|そだ}てておきたい。
examples.english: I want to train young people so the work continues even when I am gone.

examples.japanese: {我|われ}を{忘|わす}れて{見|み}とれた。
examples.english: I was so absorbed in the sight that I forgot myself.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}を{呼|よ}ばれて{我|われ}に{返|かえ}った。
examples.english: Hearing my name called, I came to my senses.

examples.japanese: {皆|みな}が{我|われ}も{我|われ}もと{席|せき}を{立|た}ち、{出口|でぐち}に{向|む}かって{走|はし}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Everyone leapt up, each trying to be first, and ran for the exit.

notes:
USAGE:
Outside set phrases, {我|われ} is confined to formal writing and oratory; using it in conversation sounds archaic or theatrical. The plural {我々|われわれ} (we), by contrast, is ordinary formal speech.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {我|われ}に{返|かえ}る: to come to one's senses
- {我|われ}を{忘|わす}れる: to be beside oneself; to be lost in something
- {我|われ}も{我|われ}も: everyone at once, each pushing to be first
- {我|われ}こそは: I am the one — declaring oneself equal to a task
- {我|わ}が{国|くに}: our country — the same kanji read わ before が

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {私|わたし}: I — the neutral everyday pronoun
- {自分|じぶん}: oneself — the ordinary word for sense 2
